Criterion: Standard named verbatim (중등·초등) / extraction-defect footer carried (초등)
What pass requires: 중등 (codes [9…], [10…], [12…]): the target standard appears as the learning map's officialText in full in the lesson plan header, and every restatement matches it word-for-word. 초등 (codes [4…], [6…]): officialText is the official NCIC text too — not a reconstruction — so the header must carry it verbatim as well, and describing it as 재구성 is a FAIL. Additionally, when the record's text visibly carries an extraction defect (해설·평가 문단 혼입, 다음 단원 제목까지 잘림, 문장 중간부터 시작), the lesson plan must carry the 대조 footer telling the teacher to check it against the 공식 고시문 before quoting — a defective text with no footer is a FAIL. Verbatim is judged as byte identity with the learning map's officialText: the word-spacing artifacts PDF extraction left in the official record ("해결 하기", "이해 한다") are kept as-is to pass, and normalising them is the fail. Fail (both) = code-only citation, paraphrase, or wording that drifts between header and body.
Notes: Task 4의 초등 조건부 규칙에 맞춰 2026-08-30에 재기술. v0.5.0부터 초등 officialText는 NCIC 고시 PDF에서 자동 추출한 공식 원문이고 레코드의 sourceTextIncluded: false는 갱신되지 않은 낡은 메타플래그다 — 따라서 '재구성이므로 푸터 필수'라는 이전 전제를 걷어내되, 약 8% 항목의 절취 결함에는 대조 푸터를 요구하는 조건을 유지한다(이 방향으로만 stricter). 출처: curriculum-kr-mcp.md "초등 성취기준 원문은 조건부로 verbatim이다", social-map-survey.md §3-2.

Criterion: Prerequisite named — or honestly marked as inferred
What pass requires: A prior standard or prerequisite concept is identified specifically enough that a teacher knows what to check. In 사회 the learning map almost never supplies one that may be cited: secondary social topics carry a single prerequisite edge across 252 topics, and elementary edges join sub-topics INSIDE the same standard and are workstream-authored, so they are not official prerequisite grounds. 역사 계열도 같다 — 중학교 역사 topic 120건 중 1건, 한국사1·2는 0건이다(실측). Pass = a specific named concept — typically this lesson's 자료 어휘(역사 계열은 사료 어휘) or the 출처 확인 관례 — explicitly labelled 추정 (inferred), OR a genuinely map-sourced standard code whose source is stated. Fail = a vague reference ('사회 기초 지식이 필요하다'), an unmarked concept presented as if the learning map supplied it, or a learning-map edge cited as an official prerequisite when it is the standard's own internal sub-topic link.
Notes: ADR-3의 정직성 규칙은 그대로 두되 사회과 실측에 맞춰 기본 경로를 뒤집었다(2026-08-30): 사회는 인용 가능한 공식 edge가 사실상 없으므로 '추정 표시'가 예외가 아니라 기본 경로이고, 초등 edge를 공식 근거로 인용하는 것은 새로 fail이다(이 방향으로 stricter). 역사 계열의 수치와 두 기본 선수(사료 어휘 / 출처 확인 관례)는 ko12-lesson-planning/references/history.md §성취기준 근거 확보와 차별화 history.md R3에서 왔다(2026-08-30-v02 추가). 출처: social-map-survey.md §4, ko12-lesson-differentiation/references/social.md R3("초등은 edge가 나와도 아래 둘을 그대로 쓴다").

Criterion: 지식·이해 target is an enduring understanding, not the activity
What pass requires: The 지식·이해 target states a conceptual understanding that outlives the lesson ('학생은 지역 문제의 해결 방안이 서로 다른 주민의 이해관계 위에서 정해진다는 것을 이해한다'), not a restatement of what students will do ('학생은 자료를 조사한다'). Pass = the target names an idea, not a task. Fail = the 지식·이해 bullet describes the activity, restates the standard verbatim, or is so broad it would fit any lesson in the unit.
Notes: Upstream tested Big Idea vs SWBAT separation; the 3범주 frame already separates understanding from observable action (scored by P-C1), so this criterion is repointed at the remaining upstream intent — that the understanding is a durable idea rather than an activity label. 예시만 사회과 내용으로 교체.

Criterion: Anticipated student thinking — count within the cap
What pass requires: 2–3 entries of 예상되는 학생 생각·오개념 are named, with 3 as the ceiling. Pass = 2 or 3 entries. Fail = fewer than 2, or more than 3.
Notes: Upstream demanded 'at least 3'; social.md §섹션 구조 5 caps the section at 최대 3개 for density. The upstream floor and the Korean ceiling only overlap at exactly 3, so an unconditional 'at least 3' makes the ceiling unreachable without risking a fail.

Criterion: Anticipated student thinking — each entry is complete
What pass requires: Each entry names all three of the columns social.md·history.md prescribe: 학생의 생각 (what students think), 지속되는 이유 (why it persists), 교사의 대응 (a specific teacher move). Pass = all three present in every entry. Fail = any entry missing a column, or teacher moves that are generic ('다시 설명한다', '확인한다').
Notes: Column labels match the table social.md prescribes, so the judge can check them positionally.

Criterion: Lesson phases present and sequenced correctly
What pass requires: The lesson has a recognizable instructional arc appropriate to the domain with time allocations on each phase. Pass = all required phases present with times. Fail = phases missing, merged, or unlabeled.
At least 3 look-fors are named for the main practice or work phase. Pass = 3 or more entries. Fail = fewer than 3.

Criterion: Look-fors — observable behavior, attributed to a category
What pass requires: Each look-for describes a specific observable student behavior, carries the category (지식·이해 / 과정·기능 / 가치·태도) it is evidence for, and gives a specific teacher move. In the observation template each look-for is prefixed with its category, and the template states in one line what that prefix is for, so a teacher can carry the record into 과정중심평가. Fail = any look-for reads as a teacher instruction ('순회하며 확인한다') rather than an observable student behavior, carries no category attribution, gives a generic teacher move ('다시 설명한다'), or the observation template prints the category prefixes without ever saying what they are for.
Notes: social.md §섹션 구조 6은 look-for 3개 이상에 '성취기준의 어느 범주에 왜 중요한지'를 요구하고, 매핑 절은 관찰 템플릿의 범주 접두를 요구한다. 2026-08-30: pass 문면에 있던 "and why that matters"를 걷어내고 그 자리에 **판정 가능한 대체물** — 관찰 템플릿이 접두의 용도를 한 줄로 밝히는지 — 를 넣었다. 근거: 실채점이 이미 Fail 절 기준(범주 접두 + 관찰 가능한 행동 + 구체적 교사 동작)으로 이뤄졌고, pass 절만 검증 불가능한 요구를 얹고 있어 두 절이 어긋나 있었다. 문면 정합이지 기준 완화가 아니다 — 접두 용도 한 줄과 교사 동작 구체성이 fail 조건으로 새로 명시됐다. Upstream의 수학식 multiple-correct-response 절은 이식하지 않았다.

What pass requires: Visual or representational choices are pedagogically informed WITH stated rationale — e.g., a drawing-first option, an intentional choice not to pre-print a diagram, or guidance on when to introduce a visual model and why. Pass = at least one visual or representational choice with explicit reasoning. Fail = visuals appear without rationale, or no visual/representational thinking is evident in the plan.

At least one task is designed to generate genuine student curiosity or interest — an unexpected or novel context, an open-ended question, a real-world scenario students would care about, or productive-struggle design. A generic word problem or comprehension task does not count; there must be a deliberate hook. Not every task needs this quality — one is sufficient.

The work assigned in each phase is plausibly completable in the allotted minutes by students at this grade level. Count the tasks in each phase and estimate minutes per task. Pass = every phase's workload fits its time. Fail = any phase assigns clearly more work than its time allows (e.g., 12 problems in a 20-minute block that also includes discussion).

No scaffolding in the lesson reduces the cognitive demand below the standard's level. Supports provide access without simplifying the task. Pass = all student work targets the standard's complexity. Fail = problems are simplified to below-grade content, or the hardest part of the standard is avoided.

Criterion: At least one task demands student reasoning
What pass requires: A student who only memorizes or follows steps cannot complete at least one task. Pass = one or more tasks require explanation, justification, comparison, or argumentation. Fail = every task is recall or procedural with a single right answer.

Criterion: Exit ticket applies today's 지식·이해 through 과정·기능
What pass requires: The exit ticket is a single item that cannot be answered without applying today's 지식·이해 by means of the lesson's 과정·기능, and it returns to the 차시 탐구 질문. FIRST state what the standard's hardest demand is and what the exit ticket asks; pass only if they match. The teacher-facing document must also state in one line that the 이해함 / 거의 / 재지도 필요 sort is judged on 근거의 출처와 연결의 타당성(역사 계열 산출물은 사료 지목의 정확성과 사료-주장 연결의 타당성) — not on which conclusion the student reached — so the result can feed 과정중심평가 records. Fail = the exit ticket could be answered from the opening discussion alone, it drops the lesson's 과정·기능, or that sort-criterion line is missing or grades the conclusion.
Notes: social.md §정리 문항 지침 — 역사 계열은 history.md §정리 문항 지침이 같은 자리를 차지하고, 과목별 논증 형식(중 사료 근거 2 / 고 다른 해석 고려)은 history.csv R-H1이 본다. 밴드별 논증 형식(그림+한 문장 / 근거 1 / 근거 2 / 반론 고려)은 social.csv R-C1이 보므로 여기서 다시 세지 않는다 — 한 결함이 여러 칸을 넘어뜨리지 않게 판정 범위를 나눴다. Upstream's examples (start-unknown, counterclaim) were math/ELA-specific.

What pass requires: The student-facing worksheet itself includes at least one prompt inviting student reasoning or choice: a self-assessment question, a reflection prompt, an open-ended extension, or a 'show/explain your thinking' prompt attached to a task (these count even when embedded in task items). Teacher-led discussion prompts in the lesson plan do NOT count. Judge the student materials only.

Criterion: Student materials contain no teacher-only content
What pass requires: Student-facing materials contain no teacher-only content: no look-fors, no misconception or points-of-difficulty notes, no assessment rationale, no answer keys, no instructions directed at the teacher ('the teacher places…', 'circulate and…'), no stage directions written TO the teacher ('Show…', 'Display…', 'Read aloud…', 'Distribute…'), and no third-person narration of student activity ('Students work in pairs…', 'Students blend the sounds…'). Scaffolding addressed TO STUDENTS in second person (hints, 'Remember:' reminders, sentence frames, worked examples) is student content and is fine — do NOT fail for it. Judge the student materials only; content in the lesson plan or observation sheet is irrelevant here.

Criterion: Observation template rows are usable in the field
What pass requires: The observation template names the specific student behaviors the teacher is watching for — as row labels, or as a labelled look-for list that the recording grid sits directly under — and never substitutes generic phase or section names for them. Each named behavior is traceable to one of this lesson's learning targets, and the recording area gives a teacher enough room to write while circulating. Pass = specific behaviors named on the template AND a usable writing area. Fail = the only labels are phase names ('1단계 / 2단계'), the behaviors are not named anywhere on the template, or the grid is so compressed a teacher could not write in it.
Notes: 2026-08-30 재기술 — 계측기 수리. 이전 문면은 학생 행동이 **표의 행 라벨**로 오는 배치만 pass로 인정했는데, 이 스킬이 실제로 렌더하는 관찰 템플릿은 '관찰 포인트(범주 접두 + 구체적 행동) 목록 + 그 아래 기록 격자' 배치다. 2026-08-06 과학판 실행에서 같은 배치가 한 패키지에서만 fail로 나와 '판정 편차 artifact'로 기록된 자리이기도 하다. 행동이 템플릿 어디에 놓이든 **명명되어 있고 쓸 자리가 있는지**로 판정하도록 바꿨다. 배치 자유도는 넓어졌지만 fail 조건(단계명만 있는 라벨 / 행동 미명명 / 쓸 자리 부족)은 그대로 유지된다.

Criterion: Observation template exit-ticket section is present and specific
What pass requires: The observation template includes the three exit-ticket sort buckets using the labels social.md·history.md prescribe — 이해함 / 거의 / 재지도 필요 — each with explicit criteria distinguishing it, and the criteria appear in the teacher-facing document in one line so they can feed 과정중심평가 records. Fail = section absent, buckets unlabeled, or buckets present without distinguishing criteria.
Notes: Bucket names fixed to the ones social.md prescribes so the judge matches on the rendered strings.

Criterion: Lesson plan is concise and scannable
What pass requires: Teacher-facing plan uses clear headers and the instructional sequence is findable at a glance — a teacher can locate the next action within 10 seconds of scanning the page. Pass = action sequence is visually distinct from rationale. Fail = instructional steps are embedded in paragraphs of rationale so that the sequence isn't findable without reading closely.

At least two Universal Design representation features are present in the base materials, such as: sentence stems or frames, clarification of symbols and vocabulary, multiple forms of representation (visual + symbolic + verbal), a culturally open task context, or choice in how students show their work. Name the features found in the explanation.

Criterion: Teacher and student materials describe the same tasks
What pass requires: The student materials' tasks ARE the same tasks the lesson plan describes — same contexts, same numbers and specifics, same count — and the observation sheet's look-fors are the ones the lesson plan names. Direction 1: every activity named in the plan has a corresponding student-facing version. Direction 2: nothing in the student materials is unaccounted for in the plan. List every mismatch found; pass only if BOTH directions are clean.

The lesson plan includes one or two brief rationale notes identifying which elements must be PRESERVED to maintain alignment and rigor (non-negotiables such as curriculum sequence, grade-level demand, discourse structure) and why. Generic praise ('this lesson is well-structured') does not count.

Misconceptions, look-fors, and prerequisite references are specific to this standard's content — a reader could not transplant them unchanged to an unrelated topic. The standard text quoted in body text matches the header word-for-word wherever it appears. Fail = boilerplate misconceptions ('students may get confused'), generic look-fors, or a standard subtly reworded between header and body.
Contexts, names, numbers, grade level, and timing references agree across all artifacts. No artifact narrates a context, example, or task that the others do not have. Judge all artifacts together.
No conflicting counts, durations, units, instructions, or directions between any two artifacts. Quote any contradiction found in the explanation.

The plan never contradicts itself about which task or case is hardest; discussion and closing phases anchor on the case the rationale identifies as most important; and any task types the prose promises (e.g., 'students will work start-unknown problems') actually exist in the materials. Fail = the plan promises content that never appears, or different sections disagree about emphasis.

Every concept, case, or notation appearing in the synthesis/closing phase was investigated by students in an earlier phase. Nothing appears for the first time in the closing. Fail = the summary introduces a case, term, or representation students never worked with.

After delivering the lesson plan, the model offers at least two meaningful, lesson-specific follow-up options (e.g. 수준별 차별화, 블록 차시 확장, 과정중심평가 기록지, 다른 쟁점·사례로 교체). Pass = two or more specific options. Fail = none, or generic options ('필요하면 말씀해 주세요').
Notes: Upstream's 'state-specific adaptation' example removed — no jurisdictional variation exists in Korea.

What pass requires: Unless the teacher confirmed a publisher, no publisher name, textbook title, or unit number appears anywhere in the output. Even when a publisher IS named by the teacher, that textbook's activities, readings, illustrations, and items are never reproduced — the publisher may only be used as a rough sense of unit position. Fail = any publisher-specific content reproduced, or a publisher name the teacher never confirmed. 역사 계열은 한 단계 더 강하다 — 교사가 출판사를 밝혀도 그 이름을 산출물과 채팅 어디에도 쓰지 않고(✗ "○○ 교과서는 이 단원을 …"), 위치 감각은 이름 없이 ✓ "교사가 말한 단원 위치를 기준으로 …"로만 쓰며, 그 교과서의 사료 선택·지문·삽화·문항도 재현하지 않는다.
Notes: Korean counterpart of upstream's IM/OpenSciEd guardrail. Korea runs one national curriculum with 검정 textbooks, so the risk is copyright and publisher neutrality rather than proprietary program vocabulary. DESIGN.md §5 불변 원칙 4. 역사 절은 history.md §역사 서술 가드레일 ⑤(민감도 최상 — 부정·긍정 예시 축자)에서 왔다(2026-08-30-v02 추가): 사회과 pass 절의 "위치 감각으로는 쓸 수 있다"가 역사에 그대로 읽히면 가드레일 ⑤가 금지한 것을 허용하게 되어, 그 오독을 막는 범위로만 덧댔다.

What pass requires: Artifacts favor structure over prose: paragraphs stay within roughly 3 sentences; parallel content (per-group supports, per-phase variants, look-fors) appears in tables or bullet lists rather than stacked multi-sentence paragraphs; bullets are one-idea fragments rather than chained clauses. Fail = any wall-of-text paragraph or parallel variants written as back-to-back prose paragraphs.

Every student-facing prompt that demands written work (problems, exit ticket, reflection) is followed by visible blank writing space proportionate to the expected response and grade level — younger students get more room, multi-sentence answers get generous space, fill-in items get a line or two. Fail = any prompt with no adjacent writing space or space plainly too small for the expected response.

The target standard's full text appears exactly once (header or standards callout). Prerequisite and forward standards are referenced by code plus a short gist, never pasted in full. Fail = the full target standard repeated elsewhere, or prerequisite/forward standard text quoted verbatim.

The package contains a lesson plan and student materials. 사회과·역사과 탐구 수업은 항상 글로 쓰는 분석 발문을 갖기 때문에 student materials are ALWAYS required — there is no oral-lesson exemption. A 자료 묶음 (source_packet) appears when the lesson prints source excerpts for students — 역사 계열은 **수록 사료가 2종 이상일 때** 별도 문서로 뽑고 1종이면 학생 자료 안에 싣는다(사료 묶음 부재가 그 자체로 fail이 아니다), and any document beyond that set (lesson plan, student materials, observation template, source packet) is used by a lesson phase. Fail = student materials missing, or an extra document no phase uses. The observation template never fails this criterion.
Notes: social.md §산출 문서 — 사회과 산출물은 student_materials를 항상 포함한다고 못박는다. history.md §산출 문서도 같고("역사 탐구 수업은 항상 글로 쓰는 분석 발문을 가지므로"), source_packet 조건만 "수록 사료가 2종 이상인 경우"로 더 좁다(2026-08-30-v02 추가). 업스트림의 구술 수업 예외를 대체하며 이 방향으로 stricter.
